newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA data bearish for live cattle.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA data bearish for live cattle.

text.p: CME traders said that the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly Cattle on Feed report was bearish for live cattle futures.

They noted the greatest decline were likely to be seen on deferred months with July placements in the leading seven cattle-feeding states estimated at 118 percent of a year ago, much higher than analysts had expected.
December live cattle futures were seen opening 0.50 to 0.75 cent a lb lower on Monday based on the report.

October futures were expected to open down 0.25 to 0.50 cent a lb Monday with higher-than-expected July marketings in the leading seven states of 109 percent of a year ago, supportive for nearby months.
A Reuter survey of analysts had produced an average placement estimate of 100.8 percent of a year ago and an average marketings estimate of 105.5 percent in the seven primary states.
The cattle-on-feed total for the leading seven states at 119 percent of a year ago was above the average analyst estimate of 115.6 percent and above the highest analyst estimate of 117.8 percent.
